newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: APEC a success, but frets over image, official says.
newsitem.headline: APEC a success, but frets over image, official says.

text.p: The 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum is a resounding success, but it has done a terrible job explaining its achievements to its people and business community, a top official said on Tuesday.

Jack Whittleton, the APEC Secretariat's executive director, told an audience of diplomats that APEC had accomplished a lot in eliminating trade barriers and reaching agreement to implement free trade in the Asia-Pacific region by the year 2020.

"I think APEC has been doing an absolutely lousy job in explaining to the public what we have achieved," Whittleton said. "APEC needs to better articulate the benefits of its work to its private sector and general population."
"From my vantage point, APEC is succeeding. It is taking tangible steps to implement the goals set by economic leaders," he added.

Canada, which is hosting the annual summit of APEC leaders in November, wants the group to move forward in implementing its agreements on opening up key sectors of the economy like information technology, Whittleton said.
The APEC trade ministers' meeting in Montreal on May 9 and 10 will discuss measures to maintain the momentum of trade liberalisation and to trim the cost of doing business in the region.
Whittleton said: "APEC's incremental process is working, is gaining momentum and will result in tangible measures when economic leaders meet in Vancouver this November."

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
